examples.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving Exponential Functions with the Same Exponents and a Polynomial
examples.worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}{e}^{x+1}-2{e}^{x+1} & <-x{e}^{x+1} \\ {x}^{2}{e}^{x+1}+x{e}^{x+1}-2{e}^{x+1} & <0 \\ ({x}^{2}+x-2){e}^{x+1} & <0 \\ (x+2)(x-1){e}^{x+1} & <0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by $e^{x+1}$ and get

$$
(x+2)(x-1) <   0.
$$

This represents an upwards parabola whose roots are at $x=-2$ and $x=1.$ The parabola is below the $x$-axis when $-2 <   x <   1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013930/assets/2f01104ae0cb9a41c5c5e4b8393e346f7d0e9b2bfd1afa593ee6bdfb0fff39f2.png)

Therefore, the solution is $-2 <   x <   1.$

feedback.worked_solution:
When we have an inequality involving an exponential function with a positive base, we're allowed to multiply or divide both sides by the exponential function.

Dividing both sides of the given inequality by ${6}^{3x-2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(49-{x}^{2})^{3}\cdot {6}^{3x-2} & \le 0 \\ \frac{(49-{x}^{2})^{3}\cdot {6}^{3x-2}}{{6}^{3x-2}} & \le \frac{0}{{6}^{3x-2}} \\ (49-{x}^{2})^{3} & \le 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve the inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{(49-{x}^{2})^{3}} & \le \sqrt[3]{0} \\ 49-{x}^{2} & \le 0 \\ -{x}^{2} & \le -49 \\ {x}^{2} & \ge 49 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{49} \\ |x| & \ge 7\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we had to flip the sign again of the inequality since we divided by a negative number ($-1$).

Therefore, the solution to the inequality is $x\le -7$ or $x\ge 7.$
